material.text: chrismaree/open-code-mcp-on-demand: OpenCode plugin: MCP servers stay dormant until your agent needs them. Saves RAM and prompt context.
type=plugin source=github:chrismaree/open-code-mcp-on-demand created=2026-10-25T18:29:25Z firstSeen=2026-11-03T14:29:15.298Z published=? maintainers=? repoId=1433508734 stars=1 npm30d=?

Quick start · How it works · Generate your settings · Configuration · FAQ

An [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) plugin that keeps your MCP servers **off until an agent actually needs them**. By default OpenCode connects every configured MCP server for every directory you have a session in. With a handful of local servers and a few open projects that quickly becomes dozens of `node`/`npx` processes and gigabytes of RAM, and every server's instructions get added to every prompt, whether the task needs them or not. `mcp-on-demand` fixes both: | | Without | With mcp-on-demand | |---|---|---| | Local MCP processes | one set per open directory, always running | only the servers a session asked for | | Other sessions' servers | every session sees every connected server | each session sees and calls only its own | | Prompt overhead | every server's instructions, every turn | a short list of groups, plus instructions for connected servers only | | Using a server | always there | agent calls `mcp_connect("browser")`, tools appear on its next step | | Forgotten servers | run until you quit | dropped after 1 hour unused, local and remote | Real-world example from the author's machine: **~70 local MCP processes (several GB) down to 0** at idle, with 25 servers still one call away. ## Quick start **1. Install** (macOS / Linux): ```sh curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrismaree/open-code-mcp-on-demand/master/install.sh | sh ``` This copies one file, `mcp-on-demand.ts`, into `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` and creates a starter `~/.config/opencode/mcp-on-demand.json`. OpenCode loads plugins from that folder automatically. No `opencode.json` changes are needed. **2. Restart OpenCode** (or open a new session). That's it. Every MCP server is now dormant, and the agent sees them listed as "Ungrouped servers" it can connect by name. **3. Recommended: group your servers** so the agent knows *when* to use each one. Paste the prompt from [Generate your settings](#generate-your-settings) into an OpenCode session. **4. Check it:** ask the agent *"run mcp_status"*.
Manual install ```sh mkdir -p ~/.config/opencode/plugins curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrismaree/open-code-mcp-on-demand/master/mcp-on-demand.ts \ -o ~/.config/opencode/plugins/mcp-on-demand.ts ``` Or clone this repo and symlink the file: ```sh git clone https://github.com/chrismaree/open-code-mcp-on-demand.git ln -s "$PWD/open-code-mcp-on-demand/mcp-on-demand.ts" ~/.config/opencode/plugins/mcp-on-demand.ts ``` OpenCode watches the symlink, not its target, so after editing the repo copy reload with `touch -h ~/.config/opencode/plugins/mcp-on-demand.ts`.
## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph OpenCode["OpenCode (one instance per directory)"] Agent["🤖 Agent"] Plugin["⚡ mcp-on-demand"] end subgraph Servers["Your MCP servers"] A["context7
(always on)"] B["playwright
💤 dormant"] C["github
💤 dormant"] D["slack
💤 dormant"] end Plugin -- "group list in system prompt" --> Agent Agent -- "mcp_connect(['browser'])" --> Plugin Plugin -- "enable" --> B Agent -. "always available" .-> A ``` 1. **At startup** the plugin marks every configured MCP server as disabled, except those in `alwaysOn`. 2. **The agent sees a short catalog** of your groups in its system prompt, plus three tools: `mcp_connect`, `mcp_disconnect` and `mcp_status`. 3. **When a task needs a server**, the agent calls `mcp_connect` with a group or server name. The connection belongs to **that session**; OpenCode starts the server and the tools appear from the agent's next step. 4. **Sessions only see their own servers.** OpenCode runs MCP servers per directory, so a server another session connected is running, but the plugin removes it from this session's Code Mode catalog, MCP instructions and tool list, and refuses its calls with "call mcp_connect first". Subagents start lean too (see `inheritToChildSessions`). 5. **Unused servers are dropped.** A session drops a server after `idleMinutes` (default 60) without a call to it and nothing in flight; once no session holds a server, it is turned off. This applies to local and remote servers: remote ones cost no memory, but every connected server adds text to every prompt. 6. **Recovery is automatic.** If tools are missing (idle drop, restart), the agent calls `mcp_connect` again. It's safe to repeat. ### A server's lifecycle ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Dormant: plugin loads Dormant --> Connected: a session calls mcp_connect Connected --> Connected: that session's tool calls reset its idle timer Connected --> Dormant: the last session holding it disconnects Connected --> Dormant: unused for idleMinutes by every session holding it Dormant --> Connected: agent reconnects when tools are missing ``` ### Under the hood It's a single file built only on OpenCode's native V2 plugin API: no proxy, gateway or extra process. | Need | OpenCode plugin API | |---|---| | Turn servers on and off | `ctx.mcp.transform` + `ctx.mcp.reload()` | | Agent-facing tools | `ctx.tool.transform` | | Group catalog in the prompt; per-session filtering of the catalog, MCP instructions and tools | `ctx.session.hook("context")` | | Usage tracking and per-session call checks (Code Mode reports each MCP call under the server's tool name) | `ctx.tool.hook("execute.before" / "execute.after")` | | Per-directory server state, per-session connections | `ctx.location.directory`, the hooks' `sessionID` | ## Generate your settings Your settings depend on which MCP servers *you* have, so there's nothing to copy. Let your agent write them. Paste this into an OpenCode session: > Read my OpenCode MCP configuration (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, any project `opencode.json` / `.opencode/opencode.json`) and run `mcp_status` to see every MCP server I have. Then write `~/.config/opencode/mcp-on-demand.json` following the schema of https://github.com/chrismaree/open-code-mcp-on-demand/blob/master/mcp-on-demand.example.json: > > - Put a server in `alwaysOn` only if it is cheap and useful in almost every session (for example docs lookup or memory). Keep this list short. > - Group the rest by **task**: when would someone need it, not who makes it. Aim for 4–12 groups and keep servers that are usually used together in one group. > - Give each group one specific sentence saying what it gives access to and when to use it. The agent reads these descriptions to decide what to connect. > - Use the exact server names from my config. > - Never copy URLs, headers, API keys, tokens or any other secrets into this file. > > Show me the result before saving it. Afterwards, apply it with `touch ~/.config/opencode/plugins/mcp-on-demand.ts`. ## Configuration `~/.config/opencode/mcp-on-demand.json` (see [`mcp-on-demand.example.json`](mcp-on-demand.example.json)): ```jsonc { "enabled": true, // false = plugin does nothing, servers keep their configured state "alwaysOn": ["context7"], // never made dormant "idleMinutes": 60, // a session drops a server it has not used for this long "inheritToChildSessions": false, // subagents start without their parent's servers "groups": { "browser": { "description": "Browser automation: open pages, click, fill forms, take screenshots.", "servers": ["playwright", "chrome-devtools"] } }, "autoConnect": [ // connect groups automatically in matching directories { "directory": "~/work/my-web-app*", "groups": ["browser"] } ] } ``` | Key | Default | Notes | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `true` | Set `false` to switch the plugin off without uninstalling. | | `alwaysOn` | `[]` | Server names that are never touched. | | `idleMinutes` | `60` | A session drops a server after this long without a call to it (nothing in flight). A server stops once no session holds it. Local and remote alike. | | `inheritToChildSessions` | `false` | `true`: a child session (subagent) starts with its parent's servers. `false`: it starts lean and connects what it needs. | | `localIdleHours`, `localIdleMinutes` | — | Deprecated; read only when `idleMinutes` is not set. | | `groups` | `{}` | Group name → `{ description, servers }`. Servers not in a group are still dormant and connectable by name. | | `autoConnect` | `[]` | Groups every new session in a matching directory starts with. `directory` matches the directory and its subdirectories; `*` matches within one path segment. | **Applying changes:** run `touch ~/.config/opencode/plugins/mcp-on-demand.ts`. The plugin reloads; editing only the JSON is not picked up. Reloading resets on-demand connections, and agents reconnect as needed. **Alternatives:** settings can also be passed as plugin `options` in `opencode.json` (they override the file), and `OPENCODE_MCP_ON_DEMAND_CONFIG` points at a different settings path. ### Adding a new MCP server Add it to OpenCode as usual (`opencode mcp add …`). It starts **dormant automatically** and is listed to the agent as ungrouped. Optionally add it to a group with a description, or to `alwaysOn`, then touch the plugin file. ## Agent tools | Tool | What it does | |---|---| | `mcp_connect({ targets })` | Connects groups or servers for the current session, waits until they're connected and lists their tools. Idempotent. | | `mcp_disconnect({ targets })` | Drops them for the current session; a server stops once no session holds it. | | `mcp_status()` | Lists groups and every server's state for this session: always-on, connected, held by another session, or dormant. | ## FAQ **What happens if the plugin breaks?** It only changes server state at runtime and never edits `opencode.json`. If it fails to load, every server keeps its configured state, so you're back to stock behaviour instead of missing tools. **Why does a tool appear one step late?** OpenCode snapshots the tool list per model request, so tools from a newly connected server appear on the agent's next step. The `mcp_connect` result tells the agent this. **Do connections affect other sessions?** No. OpenCode runs MCP servers per directory, but each session only sees and calls the servers it connected. One gap: Code Mode's built-in `search(...)` can still list another session's tool names; calling them is refused. **Does reconnecting cost anything?** One `mcp_connect` call. Connecting or dropping a server changes this session's prompt, so its next request reads the conversation again instead of using the provider's prompt cache. After an hour away the cache has usually expired anyway. **A server shows as disabled even after `mcp_connect`?** `mcp_connect` checks OpenCode's actual server state and reloads whenever a requested server is not enabled, then retries once if it is still disabled, so a stale view in the plugin cannot leave a server stuck. Servers that failed or need sign-in are reported as such; reloading would not fix them. **What if OpenCode changes how it renders the catalog?** The filters only remove blocks they recognise exactly (`- name (N tools …)` catalog entries and `` instruction blocks). Anything else is left as is, so a format change means extra text in the prompt, never a broken one. Calls to other sessions' servers are still refused. **Is state lost when a local server stops?** Yes. A restarted server starts fresh (for example, an open browser page is gone). Raise `idleMinutes`, or keep such a server in `alwaysOn`, if that matters. **Where are the logs?** `~/.local/share/opencode/log/mcp-on-demand.log`: loads, connects, tool use, refused calls and idle drops, each with its session. **Uninstall?** `rm ~/.config/opencode/plugins/mcp-on-demand.ts` (and optionally `~/.config/opencode/mcp-on-demand.json`), then restart OpenCode. ## Compatibility Built for the **OpenCode V2 plugin API**, tested on OpenCode v2.1.2. Tests for the prompt filters: `npm test` (`node --test test/*.test.ts`) (Node 22.18+ runs TypeScript directly). Related upstream discussions: [lazy MCP loading (#8277)](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/8277) and [duplicate MCP processes per session (#29939)](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/29939). If OpenCode ships native lazy loading, this plugin may become unnecessary. ## License [MIT](LICENSE)
